title: What the 50-acre expansion of Innovation Park's growth boundary means for Penn State - NewsBreak
text:
9 hours ago Innovation Park at Penn State on Monday, March 31, 2025. Abby Drey/adrey@centredaily.com The Centre Region Council of Governments’ General Forum unanimously approved a 50-acre expansion of Innovation Park’s regional growth boundary last week. The move clears the way for Penn State to build a unified 88-acre campus for its Applied Research Laboratory over the next 50 years.
FULL STORY: 50-acre growth boundary expansion will allow Penn State to unify, enlarge ARL campus
Here are key takeaways:
The expansion will create a unified campus for ARL, which is currently spread across the southwest corner of Penn State’s University Park campus and other smaller offices. All on-campus ARL employees will gradually move to the new site as buildings are constructed in the coming years. Construction is already underway on a $91.1 million, 80,000-square-foot ARL building at 335 Innovation Blvd. ARL Director of Engineering Rachel Prinkey said it should be completed by June 2027. College Township Council member Eric Bernier said the expansion is a logical extension of Innovation Park and does not promote outward sprawl, noting the area was envisioned for similar use 25 years ago. State College Borough Council member Matt Herndon pushed back on that characterization, saying the project moves hundreds or thousands of jobs farther from housing and makes biking and transit access harder. The ARL is one of only five U.S. Navy-sponsored university-affiliated research centers in the country, employs more than 1,500 people and conducts roughly $415 million in annual research. The summary points above were compiled with the help of AI tools and edited by journalists. The full story in the link at top was reported, written and edited entirely by journalists.
